title: Why cheap things are more expensive
description: Two people buy boots. Ten years later the one who spent more has spent less. The boots theory, in forty seconds.

scenes.say: Two people buy boots. One spends fifty. One spends ten.
Ten years later, the one who spent fifty has spent less.
The cheap boots last one winter. So you buy them again. And again. Ten winters, ten pairs, one hundred pounds.
The good boots last ten years. Fifty pounds, once.
So the person who could afford the better boots paid half as much for exactly the same thing.
This is the quiet unfairness of being short of money. The real price of a thing is not what it costs. It is what it costs per year.
